newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to amend portfolio taxation rules.
newsitem.headline: Romania to amend portfolio taxation rules.

text.p: Romania's government has altered a proposed law on portfolio investment, replacing a four percent tax on capital gains with a 1.5 percent tax on each portfolio transaction, the Reform Minister said on Monday.
"We revised the rules last night...We decided to charge 1.5 percent of the value of each deal," Ulm Spineanu told Reuters by telephone.
A government official said the latest amendments would be discussed by the government and be published in the Official Gazette before becoming effective.

Adoption of a law on portfolio investment had been viewed as a critical measure in pressing forward with the new centrist government's reforms and attracting the interest of previously uneasy Western investors.

The proposed law was first announced last week, coinciding with a monitoring mission to Bucharest by the International Monetary Fund and discussions by the World Bank board in Washington on releasing credits.

The pro-government daily Romania Libera on Monday published the latest amended version of the rules. It showed the four percent capital gains tax and another 0.1 percent extra tax on short-term flows had been replaced by a single tax of 1.5 percent charged for each deal.
"We decided to have a single tax as a simple rule seems more favourable for foreign investors and it is easier to monitor," Spineanu said.
Spineanu had initially presented the rules during a news conference last Wednesday and a government statement issued then had said the rules were approved.
He told Reuters the latest amendment was intended to alleviate fears that a capital gains tax might act as a barrier when investors left the market.

Western lenders and investors last week praised the move to issue portfolio investment rules and hailed the four percent tax as attractive. Volumes and turnover levels on the Bucharest bourse and the over-the-counter market soared. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
